trainee_content: Stage 3 isn't a one-and-done lesson — it's a body of leadership material you'll keep returning to. Learn WHERE to pull from: this module library, the Toolkit PDFs, your own coach, your peers, and the founders' content. The leaders who plateau are the ones who stop sourcing new material; the ones who keep climbing read, watch, and ask in equal measure.
what_good_looks_like: Knows the 4-5 places leadership material lives (toolkit, library, peers, founders, books)
Carries a current 'one thing I'm working on' from a recent source
References specific material in their coaching with junior leaders
how_measured: Self-reported reading / watching / listening cadence
Quality of references in 1-on-1s
Visible upgrade in a single skill quarter-over-quarter
leader_coaching_notes: Hand them a curated list — don't make them search blind
Ask in every 1-on-1: what are you sourcing this week?
Praise application of new material publicly

trainee_content: As a new BA, your coach provided motivation. At Stage 3, you provide it for yourself AND your team — every single day. Self-motivated leaders don't outsource their mood to weather, the team, or yesterday. They treat motivation as a skill: morning state-routine, written goals, evidence files of past wins. Action creates motivation, not the other way around.
what_good_looks_like: Arrives ready to lead every day, regardless of personal mood
Has a written long-term goal they can articulate in one sentence
Doesn't blame external factors for poor weeks
Can lift the room's energy when it dips
how_measured: Consistent week-over-week effort — no "off weeks"
Team energy stays high on tough field days
Self-review reflects ownership, not blame
leader_coaching_notes: Help them connect numbers to a goal they emotionally own
Show them their own track record of recovery from bad days
Catch and correct "I'm just not feeling it" language

assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate self-motivation when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies self-motivation reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives self-motivation without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Accountability is the foundation of leadership. Without it, all you have is friendships. Self: own outcomes not effort, ask 'what did I miss?' before 'who failed?', hold the standard you ask of others — first. Others: set expectations crystal-clear up front, address slips early/private/with empathy, praise behaviour you want to see, correct what you don't. Silence is permission.
what_good_looks_like: Owns mistakes publicly, fixes them privately
Has uncomfortable conversations within 24 hours
Standards on the team are visible and consistent
Team members know the standard instead of guessing
how_measured: Tough conversations happen and don't damage relationships
Team behaviour aligns to stated standards within 1-2 weeks
Leader is willing to escalate, not just observe
leader_coaching_notes: Role-play tough conversations BEFORE they happen
Coach on language — "I noticed X, what's going on?"
Watch for accountability-avoidance disguised as 'being nice'

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain accountability — for self and others in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate accountability — for self and others when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies accountability — for self and others reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives accountability — for self and others without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Growth lives outside the comfort zone — and as a leader, you have to model leaving yours regularly. Pick ONE growth edge per quarter (cold-call recruiting, public speaking at meetings, holding a hard 1-on-1, running a sector you've never owned) and put yourself there on purpose. Your team will follow your willingness to be uncomfortable long before they follow your sentences about it.
what_good_looks_like: Names their current growth edge clearly
Voluntarily takes on stretch assignments
Doesn't hide behind 'that's not my strength'
Encourages teammates to step outside their comfort zone
how_measured: Visible quarterly growth-edge with measurable progress
Stretch assignments completed, not just attempted
Team culture rewards trying, not just succeeding
leader_coaching_notes: Set a quarterly comfort-zone goal WITH them
Celebrate the attempt, not just the outcome
Reframe failure as data, not identity

assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate comfort zones when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies comfort zones reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives comfort zones without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: How you show up signals what you stand for before you say a word. Image isn't vanity — it's the visual shorthand your team and supporters use to decide if you're worth following. Dress code, posture, confidence in your voice, what your phone screen looks like in a meeting: every detail compounds into the question 'do I want to be like this person?'
what_good_looks_like: Dresses, speaks, and carries themselves like the leader they want to be
Personal brand consistent across field, office, social media
New BAs say "I want to be like them" without prompting
how_measured: Image audit (peer or coach feedback) every quarter
First-impression feedback from new starters
Social-media presence aligned with role
leader_coaching_notes: Give specific image feedback — what works, what doesn't
Audit their phone/social presence with permission
Hold the line on dress-code without nagging

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain image in a coaching conversation

assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies image reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives image without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Leaders who plan run light, productive weeks. Leaders who don't run reactive, exhausting ones. Plan TIME (Sunday weekly review, daily debrief), PEOPLE (1-on-1 cadence, 1-up reviews), and PRIORITIES (what's the ONE thing this week needs?). A planned week beats a 'busy' week every time.
what_good_looks_like: Has a written weekly plan every Sunday/Monday
Plans 1-on-1s in advance with a written agenda
Knows the ONE most important thing for the week
Replans mid-week when reality shifts
how_measured: Weekly plan visible in their tool of choice
1-on-1 agendas exist (not just "we'll catch up")
Output trends up week-over-week
leader_coaching_notes: Share your own weekly plan template
Audit their plan in a Monday huddle
Praise replanning — it's a skill, not a failure

assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies planning reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives planning without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: By Stage 3, your network IS your career insurance. Build relationships with peers in other offices, leaders at later stages, partners, and supporters who become advocates. The leaders who run the biggest teams are the ones with the deepest network — they get the best recruits, the warmest leads, and the smartest counsel.
what_good_looks_like: Maintains a list of 30+ active business relationships
Reaches out monthly with no ask attached
Brings value first, asks second
Connects others without expecting credit
how_measured: Network growth tracked quarter-over-quarter
Inbound asks (people seeking THEM out) increases
Recruits/leads sourced from network
leader_coaching_notes: Coach the give-first mindset
Help them build a follow-up cadence
Make warm intros to your own network

assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate developing business relationships when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies developing business relationships reliably week-over-week, not just once

trainee_content: Recruiting is sales applied to people. Pipeline: Sourcing → Pre-screen → Day-1 Show → Day-3 Stay → Stage 1 Complete. If you understand drop-off rates between each step, you can predict who you'll have on the team in 30 days. If you don't track them, you're hoping.
what_good_looks_like: Can quote their own pipeline drop-off rates
Recruits weekly, not just when the team thins
Day-1 show rate is tracked and improving
how_measured: Pipeline tracker is current
New starters per month meet the agreed quota
30-day retention at or above office average
leader_coaching_notes: Coach the FUNNEL, not individual Initial Appointments
Tie weekly recruiting activity to monthly team size
Review drop-offs — where are people leaving?

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain understanding the process / pipeline in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate understanding the process / pipeline when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies understanding the process / pipeline reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives understanding the process / pipeline without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Every recruiting conversation hinges on whether the candidate buys the BUSINESS CONCEPT — what we actually do, why it works, and where it can take them. Get yours tight: a 60-second story, a 2-minute explanation, and a 10-minute deep-dive. The right candidate self-selects in; the wrong one self-selects out.
what_good_looks_like: Has a 60-second concept pitch they can deliver cleanly
Adapts the pitch to different candidate backgrounds
Doesn't oversell or undersell the model
Lets the candidate ask, doesn't lecture
how_measured: Concept pitch tested in roleplay with their coach
Candidate-conversion rate at the concept stage
Quality of self-screening from candidates
leader_coaching_notes: Roleplay the concept pitch, then watch a live one
Coach honesty — overpromised candidates wash out
Track which version of the pitch works for which background

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain business concept in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate business concept when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies business concept reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives business concept without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Your team's network is your warmest pipeline. A leader who builds a referral culture gets recruits at a fraction of the cost of cold sourcing — and the referrals retain better. Make referrals a public, rewarded, repeated ask. 'Who's the best person you know?' should be a normal Monday question.
what_good_looks_like: Asks every team member for referrals at least monthly
Has a written referral incentive that's actually paid
Tracks referrals → starts → 30-day retention
Celebrates referrers publicly
how_measured: % of new starters from referrals (target 30%+)
Referrer-retention link tracked
Referral incentive paid on time, every time
leader_coaching_notes: Make the ask normal in team meetings
Pay incentives the day they're earned — speed = trust
Highlight stories: 'X referred Y, who's now top 3'

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain team referrals in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate team referrals when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies team referrals reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives team referrals without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Recruiting KPIs aren't decoration — they're the early warning system for next quarter's team size. Critical numbers: weekly sourcing reach, pre-screens booked, Day-1 show, Day-3 stay, Stage-1 graduate rate. Know yours cold and trend them weekly. When sales dip, sales is usually a recruiting problem from 60 days ago.
what_good_looks_like: Can recite all 5 recruiting KPIs from memory
Reviews KPIs weekly with their coach
Spots trends 2-3 weeks before they hit team size
Adjusts behaviour off the numbers, not gut feel
how_measured: KPI dashboard exists and is updated weekly
Recruiting health predicted forward 30-60 days
Bad numbers trigger plan changes within 1 week
leader_coaching_notes: Make KPIs visible in shared docs
Weekly review every Monday — 5 minutes is enough
Coach the lead-indicator mindset

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain understanding your kpis in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate understanding your kpis when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies understanding your kpis reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives understanding your kpis without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Set expectations BEFORE Day 1, not after. New recruits who walk in clear on hours, dress, attitude, and the first-week milestones quit far less often than those who get blindsided. Write it down, send it ahead, repeat it on Day 1. Clarity is kindness.
what_good_looks_like: Sends a written 'Day 1 Welcome' before the first day
Restates expectations clearly on Day 1 in person
Covers hours, dress, attitude, and first-week goals
Confirms understanding — doesn't just lecture
how_measured: Day-1-to-Day-2 retention above 80%
New starters can repeat the expectations back
Welcome doc exists and is sent every time
leader_coaching_notes: Audit their welcome doc — sharpen it once a quarter
Watch a Day-1 expectation conversation in person
Track which expectations get missed most often

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain expectations for a new recruit in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate expectations for a new recruit when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies expectations for a new recruit reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives expectations for a new recruit without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Hosting is the small, deliberate hospitality acts that make a Day 1 feel like 'I want to be here'. Greet them at the door (don't make them stand awkward), introduce them to 2-3 teammates by name, walk them through where things are, set up their phone/tools BEFORE they arrive. Hosting is 10 minutes that buys you 10 days of retention.
what_good_looks_like: Greets every new starter personally on Day 1
Introduces them to specific teammates by name
Has tools, badges, materials ready in advance
Treats them like a guest until they feel part of the team
how_measured: Day-1 NPS survey (informal feedback works)
30-day retention vs. office average
New starters report feeling welcomed
leader_coaching_notes: Model great hosting in front of them once
Pre-prep checklist for every Day 1
Praise the small acts — others will copy them

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain hosting in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate hosting when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies hosting reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives hosting without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Day 1 makes or breaks retention. A new person who has a bad Day 1 rarely makes it to Day 6. A great Day 1 isn't about lots of sign-ups — it's about CONFIDENCE (they tried something new and survived), CLARITY (they know what's expected on Day 2), and CONNECTION (they trust you and the team).
what_good_looks_like: Has a written plan before the new starter arrives
Spends Day 1 on confidence, not metrics
Doesn't overload with information
Ends Day 1 with a clear Day 2 commitment
how_measured: New starter returns for Day 2
Day 1 plan document exists and was followed
New starter can repeat what's expected of them tomorrow
leader_coaching_notes: Coach leaders to plan BEFORE the day, not improvise during
Watch a Day 1 in-field — most leaders over-coach
Track Day-1-to-Day-2 retention as a leadership KPI

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain 1st day coaching plan in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate 1st day coaching plan when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies 1st day coaching plan reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives 1st day coaching plan without admin or peer prompting

topic: What Impacts to Coach and When
trainee_content: Week one isn't 'coach everything' — it's 'coach the 2-3 things that move the needle THIS week and save the rest for later'. Day 1-2: open + posture. Day 3-4: pitch flow + objections. Day 5-6: closes + follow-up. Premature coaching on advanced skills overwhelms; staged coaching builds.
what_good_looks_like: Knows what to coach on each day of week 1
Doesn't pile advanced skills on a Day 2 new starter
Adapts the staging when a new starter is ahead/behind
Documents what was coached on which day
how_measured: New starter skill progression maps to expected day
Coaching log exists per new starter
Week-one feedback survey shows 'right pace'
leader_coaching_notes: Provide a week-one coaching map / checklist
Audit their coaching pace mid-week
Push back when they over-coach

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain what impacts to coach and when in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate what impacts to coach and when when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies what impacts to coach and when reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives what impacts to coach and when without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: When a new starter struggles, most leaders coach the SYMPTOM (their close ratio is low) instead of the CURE (their open is rushed, so supporters go cold by close). Diagnose 2 levels deep before you teach. Watch a full conversation, find the actual root cause, then coach there. Symptom-coaching wastes both your time and theirs.
what_good_looks_like: Watches full conversations before coaching
Diagnoses 2-3 levels before correcting
Coaches the cause, not just the visible failure
Tracks whether the cure actually fixes the symptom
how_measured: New starter improvement after coaching is measurable
Repeat-issue rate drops over 2-3 weeks
Coaching notes show diagnosis, not just observation
leader_coaching_notes: Run a 'find the cure' exercise live in field
Drill them on common symptom→cure mappings
Praise diagnosis quality, not just delivery

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain symptom vs cure in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate symptom vs cure when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies symptom vs cure reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives symptom vs cure without admin or peer prompting

topic: Dividing Time Between Selling and Coaching
trainee_content: The hardest tension in week one: you have personal numbers AND a new starter. The wrong split kills either your week (over-coach) or their retention (under-coach). Default rule: 60% coaching the first two days, 40% by Day 4, 25% by Day 6. Plan it; don't wing it.
what_good_looks_like: Has a written time split per week-one day
Hits personal minimums while still coaching
Doesn't disappear into selling on tough days
Adjusts split based on new starter readiness
how_measured: Personal numbers don't collapse during week one
New starter retention stays at office target
Self-reported 'time on the new starter' matches plan
leader_coaching_notes: Audit their split mid-week
Coach the trade-off explicitly: "this week you'll dip 10%"
Don't reward leaders who hit numbers but lose new starters

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain dividing time between selling and coaching in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate dividing time between selling and coaching when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies dividing time between selling and coaching reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives dividing time between selling and coaching without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Confidence in week one isn't built by big wins — it's built by small repeated successes. Find one thing the new starter did well TODAY and name it specifically. End every day with a confidence-builder, not a critique. Confidence is the fuel for Day 2; without it, they don't come back.
what_good_looks_like: Names a specific win for the new starter every day
Ends each day on a positive note
Doesn't fake-praise — keeps it specific and honest
Confidence-builds even on tough days
how_measured: New starter energy at end-of-day stays high
Day-2-onward show rate above 80%
New starter can name one thing they did well that day
leader_coaching_notes: Model end-of-day confidence builders in front of them
Coach specificity over generic 'well done'
Watch for fake-praise drift

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain building confidence in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate building confidence when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies building confidence reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives building confidence without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Stage 2 is the bridge from 'doing what the coach says' to 'making your own decisions'. Set the expectation up front: more independence, more ownership, more standard. The BA who walks into Stage 2 knowing the bar will reach it; the one who's surprised by it will resist it.
what_good_looks_like: Has a written Stage 2 expectations doc
Reviews it on Day 1 of Stage 2 with the BA
Re-confirms expectations weekly during Stage 2
Holds the bar without flexing it
how_measured: Stage 2 BAs know the bar without asking
Stage 2 → Stage 3 advancement timing predictable
Resistance to standards drops over time
leader_coaching_notes: Audit their expectations doc — make it specific
Watch a Stage 2 kick-off conversation
Hold the line when leaders soften the standard

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain expectations for stage 2 in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate expectations for stage 2 when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies expectations for stage 2 reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives expectations for stage 2 without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Stage 2 days are NOT Stage 1 days with more independence — they're structurally different. Solo blocks of 30-60 min, debriefs that are question-led not lecture-led, mini-goals tied to advancement criteria. Run Stage 2 from a written daily template, not from memory.
what_good_looks_like: Has a Stage 2 daily template document
Includes solo blocks, paired blocks, debrief structure
Reviews the day with the BA using the template
Adapts the template to BA-specific gaps
how_measured: Daily template exists and is used
BA output stable across solo/paired blocks
Stage 2 → Stage 3 readiness clear by week 3
leader_coaching_notes: Share your own Stage 2 template
Audit template adherence weekly
Coach question-led debriefs hard — they default to lecture

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain stage 2 daily plan in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate stage 2 daily plan when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies stage 2 daily plan reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives stage 2 daily plan without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: By Stage 2 your role is to UN-help. The BA will resist this — they like having you there. Helping more = stunting them. Tactics: pull back physically (observe from distance, not shoulder), mirror back questions ('what would YOU do here?'), give them solo field blocks of 30-60 minutes, debrief AFTER not during.
what_good_looks_like: BAs solo-field at least 50% of the day in week 2
Coach resists stepping in mid-conversation
Debrief is question-led, not lecture-led
how_measured: BA performance on solo blocks vs. paired blocks
Coaching ratio (questions vs. statements) during debrief
BA progression to Stage 3 readiness within 3 weeks
leader_coaching_notes: Watch a debrief — count statements vs. questions
Push leaders who over-coach
Praise leaders whose BAs produce independently

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain creating independence in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate creating independence when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies creating independence reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives creating independence without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Stage 2 BAs haven't yet learned to plan their day — and a coach who doesn't TEACH planning creates BAs who burn out by Stage 3. Coach: morning route plan, midday checkpoint, end-of-day debrief. Pull-aparts, breaks, and recovery time are part of the plan, not optional.
what_good_looks_like: BAs write their own daily plan by week 2 of Stage 2
Coach audits plans without doing them for the BA
Energy/recovery windows built into the plan
Mid-day check-ins are 5 minutes, not 30
how_measured: BA can run a planned day independently
Burnout signals (energy drops, missed days) decrease
Plans become more accurate week-over-week
leader_coaching_notes: Coach the planning skill — most BAs under-plan
Audit plan vs. actual once a week
Praise replanning, not just plan-following

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain time management in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate time management when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies time management reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives time management without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Before advancing anyone to Stage 3, pretest the BA on Stage 1 and Stage 2 fundamentals. Roleplay the open. Roleplay the close. Roleplay the debrief. Make them coach a newer BA on a fundamental in front of you. If they can teach it, they own it. If they can't teach it, they can't lead it.
what_good_looks_like: Runs structured pre-advancement tests
Tests cover both Stage 1 and Stage 2 material
Includes a 'teach a newer BA' component
Doesn't advance anyone before the test is passed
how_measured: Pretest pass-rate before advancement >= 90%
Stage 3 readiness predicted from pretest score
Post-advancement failures correlate with pretest gaps
leader_coaching_notes: Run a pretest WITH them once before they run their own
Document the pretest format — make it repeatable
Don't let them skip the pretest under deadline pressure

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain pre-testing stages 1 & 2 in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate pre-testing stages 1 & 2 when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies pre-testing stages 1 & 2 reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives pre-testing stages 1 & 2 without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: Sector management is the difference between a team that produces and a team that wanders. Bad map management = wasted hours, burnt-out BAs, and missed goals. Plan the day BEFORE you arrive, don't burn the same area twice in 30 days unless it's high-density, match territory to BA skill, track which areas convert best for YOUR team.
what_good_looks_like: Sector plan written and shared before field starts
Areas tracked for performance — kept records, not memory
Backup areas pre-identified
New starters placed in the right zones
how_measured: Team sign-ups per hour on planned vs. unplanned days
Sector plan exists and is referenced
Drop in new-starter Day-1 turnoff in well-matched zones
leader_coaching_notes: Run a 10-minute map review weekly
Share office-wide territory data so they're not guessing
Coach decision-making: "Why this area today?"

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain map management in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate map management when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies map management reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives map management without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: A great sector meeting is 10-15 minutes, not 45. Cover: yesterday's wins, today's plan (turf + people + goals), the ONE thing each BA is working on, and the morale moment that ends it. Long meetings kill energy. Tight meetings build it.
what_good_looks_like: Sector meetings run under 15 minutes consistently
Cover wins, plan, focus, morale every time
Each BA leaves knowing their ONE thing for the day
Energy at end of meeting > energy at start
how_measured: Time-boxed meetings (measured)
BA recall of their ONE thing — randomly tested
Team energy / NPS post-meeting
leader_coaching_notes: Hand them an agenda template
Watch a sector meeting and timestamp it
Coach the morale-close — many leaders skip it

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain sector meetings in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate sector meetings when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies sector meetings reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives sector meetings without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: End-of-day debrief is where the week's growth lives. Most leaders rush it — the tired ones skip it entirely. Structure: Wins (specific), Misses (no blame), Learnings (per BA), Plan-tomorrow (one concrete change). 12 minutes done well > 5 minutes phoned in.
what_good_looks_like: Runs a structured EOD debrief every day
Each BA walks away with one concrete change for tomorrow
Misses are diagnosed, not blamed
Patterns surface week-over-week
how_measured: Debrief consistency (5 of 5 days)
BA growth on tracked focus areas
Patterns in the debrief inform next week's plan
leader_coaching_notes: Audit a debrief — score it on the structure
Coach the misses-without-blame mindset
Praise leaders who keep debrief discipline on tired days

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can clearly explain breaking down days in a coaching conversation
assessment_prompts.skill: Can demonstrate breaking down days when leading or coaching a teammate
assessment_prompts.consistency: Applies breaking down days reliably week-over-week, not just once
assessment_prompts.independence: Drives breaking down days without admin or peer prompting

trainee_content: You can't lead others if you don't know yourself. Self-awareness is the willingness to see yourself the way your team sees you. Three layers: knowing your emotions in the moment, knowing your patterns across days/weeks, knowing how those patterns LAND with the people you lead.
what_good_looks_like: Names emotions without judgement
Knows their own triggers and patterns
Asks for honest feedback regularly
Adjusts behaviour based on feedback
how_measured: Self-reflection journal or weekly review notes
Team feedback indicates leader is approachable
Leader can articulate their own blind spots
leader_coaching_notes: Use a 360 review at quarterly mark
Coach them through ONE specific blind spot at a time

trainee_content: Commit to giving maximum effort in every endeavour. 100% effort isn't intensity for its own sake — it's the choice to leave nothing on the table. Last knock matters as much as first. Last hour as much as first. The BAs who give 70% on tough days are the ones who plateau; the ones who keep grinding through fatigue are the ones who advance.
what_good_looks_like: Consistently demonstrates a high level of commitment, energy, and dedication
Goes through finish-line every field day, not just easy days
No "coast days" visible in their numbers
how_measured: KPI consistency week-over-week (low variance is the tell)
Last-hour productivity vs. first-hour
Coach gut-check on engagement
leader_coaching_notes: Ask: "How do you ensure you're giving your best in every situation?"
Ask: "What does 'giving 100%' mean to you in your role?"
Catch coast days early — name them privately, not publicly

trainee_content: Manage and develop your designated sales territory effectively. Territory work is half art, half discipline: know the streets, know the times, know the patterns. The BAs who treat territory like a checklist run dry quickly; the ones who treat it like a relationship build supporter pipelines that produce for years.
what_good_looks_like: Thoroughly understands their territory
Proactively engages supporters across the patch
Takes a strategic, not random, approach to growth
how_measured: Sector + door-record tracking
Repeat-supporter rate over 30 days
Heat-map of doors knocked vs. revenue
leader_coaching_notes: Review their territory plan + performance metrics
Ask: "How do you identify and prioritise opportunities within your territory?"
Ask: "What strategies do you use to cover and manage your territory?"

trainee_content: Protect your mental and emotional state, especially when things go sideways. The world will throw rude doors, bad weather, and team drama at you — your aim is to not let any of it stick. Build a reset routine: the 30-second walk, the breathing pattern, the song, whatever works. Resilience isn't avoiding the hit; it's recovering fast.
what_good_looks_like: Maintains a resilient and positive demeanour under pressure
Effectively manages stress and emotional responses
Doesn't carry one bad door to the next door
how_measured: Recovery time after a tough door (observed)
Self-report on reset rituals
Team energy contribution on hard days
leader_coaching_notes: Observe how they handle stress / negative feedback live
Ask: "What are your methods for staying resilient in challenging circumstances?"
Ask: "How do you prevent external negativity from affecting your mindset?"

trainee_content: Set clear, actionable goals — and work towards them every day. SMART goals (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound) are the spine of progress. The BAs who plateau usually have vague goals or none at all. The ones who break out have written, specific, shared, and reviewed-weekly goals — and a plan when they fall behind.
what_good_looks_like: Sets SMART goals (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound)
Actively pursues stated goals weekly
Has a recovery plan when behind, not just an excuse
how_measured: Goal sheet exists and is reviewed weekly
Goal-vs-actual gap tracked over 4-week rolling window
Adjustments visible after a miss
leader_coaching_notes: Review their set goals + progress tracking
Ask: "How do you set your goals?"
Ask: "How do you track progress, and what do you do if you're falling behind?"

trainee_content: Take ownership of your responsibilities, decisions, and outcomes. Stage 2 is the stage where BAs stop asking permission for everything and start owning their day. Take control means: make the call, own the result, fix what's broken, and don't blame the territory / weather / coach / householder. Initiative is a skill — use it daily.
what_good_looks_like: Exhibits initiative in field and team settings
Makes decisive actions when situations demand it
Takes responsibility for results — both wins and losses
how_measured: Coach observation of decision-making moments
Self-attribution language in debrief ("I" vs. "they")
Outcome ownership when things miss
leader_coaching_notes: Observe instances where they take initiative or make decisions
Ask: "Describe a situation where you took control to achieve a positive outcome."
Ask: "How do you ensure you are in control of your work and your results?"
